posts.post_title: Petechial Hemorrhages in Pig Electrical Stunning
posts.post_content: The appearance of petechial hemorrhages throughout subcutaneous tissue in pigs during electrical stunning is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Splash

Splash (also called 'muscle splashing') refers to the appearance of petechial hemorrhages (tiny pinpoint bleedings) throughout the subcutaneous tissue of pigs, caused by too high electrical current during electrical stunning.

Defects of Electrical Stunning at a Glance
  • Splash: Too high current → petechial hemorrhages in subcutaneous tissue of pigs.
  • Missed shock: Too low current → animal inadequately stunned, regains consciousness.
Prevention
  • Use correct parameters: 250 mA, 75 volts, AC, for 10 seconds.
  • Bleed the animal within 30 seconds of stunning to prevent splash.
Context: Physical Changes in Stored Meat
  • Shrinkage: loss of weight during storage.
  • Sweating: condensation of water vapour on meat brought from cold store to room temperature.
  • Loss of bloom: loss of bright red colour of fresh meat.
  • Splash — occurs at slaughter stage, not storage stage.

posts.post_title: Main Function of CO2 in Gas Stunning
posts.post_content: The main function of CO₂ in gas stunning is:

_aimcq_options.text: It causes hemorrhage of subcutaneous tissue
It causes blackening of subcutaneous tissue

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: It blocks the nerve endings

The main function of CO₂ in gas stunning is that it blocks the nerve endings in the brain, rendering the animal unconscious without pain or distress. This is why it is considered an effective and humane method for pigs.

Gas Stunning Protocol
  • Gas mixture: 70% CO₂ + 30% O₂
  • Duration: 45 seconds
  • Best suited for: Pigs
  • Commercial method for pig stunning: CO₂ gas stunning
CO₂ Does NOT Cause:
  • Hemorrhage of subcutaneous tissue — that is caused by too high electrical current (Splash).
  • Blackening of subcutaneous tissue — no such effect is associated with CO₂.
  • Denaturation of proteins — CO₂ is not a protein-denaturing agent in this context.
Comparison with Electrical Stunning
  • Electrical: AC 250 mA, 75 V, 10 sec → nerve disruption by electricity.
  • CO₂: 70% CO₂, 45 sec → chemical blockage of nerve endings.

posts.post_title: Five Rules of Neck Incision in Ritual Slaughter
posts.post_content: "Neck incision shall be completed without pause, pressure, stabbing, slanting or tearing" are the five rules of which method of ritual slaughter?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Jewish Ritual Slaughter (Schechita)

The five principles of Schechita (Jewish ritual slaughter) dictate that the neck incision must be completed without:

  1. Pause (Shehiyah)
  2. Pressure (Derasa)
  3. Stabbing (Halada)
  4. Slanting (Hagramah)
  5. Tearing (Ikur)
Key Terminology in Jewish Slaughter
  • Schochet: Butcher / the person who performs Jewish slaughter.
  • Schechita: The act of killing in Jewish slaughter.
  • Kosher: Carcass fit for Jewish consumption (stamped on brisket).
  • Terepha: Carcass unfit for Jewish consumption.
  • Puntilla: Double-edged knife used in Evernazine method (NOT Jewish).
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Halal — involves facing Mecca and reciting prayer; no 'five rules' of incision.
  • Jhatka — single blow to sever the neck; no such five-rule code.
  • Evernazine — uses Puntilla at occipito-atlantal joint; different technique entirely.

posts.post_title: Time Limit for Bleeding After Electrical Stunning
posts.post_content: Animal should be bled within how many seconds after electrical stunning to avoid muscle splashing?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 30 seconds

The animal must be bled within 30 seconds after electrical stunning to avoid muscle splashing (petechial hemorrhages in subcutaneous tissue).

Why 30 Seconds?
  • After electrical stunning, the cardiac function may still continue briefly.
  • If bleeding is delayed, blood pressure build-up can rupture small capillaries, causing 'splash' or petechial hemorrhages in the muscle and subcutaneous tissue.
  • Prompt bleeding (within 30 sec) drains the blood before capillary rupture can occur.
Sequence of Events in Humane Slaughter
  1. Stunning (creates unconsciousness) → within 30 seconds → Sticking/Bleeding.
Stunning Times (for memory)
  • Stunning duration: 30 seconds to 1 minute.
  • Post-stunning bleed time limit: 30 seconds.
  • Electrical stunning current time: 10 seconds (through brain).

posts.post_title: Light Intensity Requirements in Abattoir
posts.post_content: Recommended light intensities at inspection point, work room & chilling room are respectively:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 550 Lux, 220 Lux & 110 Lux

The recommended light intensities in an abattoir (measured at 0.9 m from floor; 1.5 m at inspection point) are:

Light Requirements in Abattoir
  • Inspection & Packing Point: 550 Lux (50 ft candle) — highest intensity for precise inspection.
  • Work Room: 220 Lux (20 ft candle) — moderate for general work.
  • Chilling Room: 110 Lux (10 ft candle) — lowest intensity needed.
Memory Tip

Inspection → Work → Chilling = 550 → 220 → 110 (halves each step: 550 ÷ 2.5 ≈ 220; 220 ÷ 2 = 110).

Other Abattoir Requirements
  • Floor gradient: 1:50 (2 cm per meter).
  • Chilling temperature: not above 7°C for carcasses, 4°C for offals.
  • Humidity of carcass chilling room: 90%.
  • Temperature of cutting room: not above 10°C.

posts.post_title: Cooked Lamb Testicles — Name
posts.post_content: Cooked testicles of lamb used as food are known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Lamb Fries

Cooked testicles specifically of lamb are called Lamb Fries.

Distinction from Similar Terms
  • Lamb Fries → Cooked testicles of lamb specifically
  • Calf Fries → One of the names for cooked testicles of calf (also called Rocky Mountain Oysters / Prairie Oysters)
  • Rocky Mountain Oysters / Prairie Oysters → Broad term for cooked testicles of calf, lamb or pig

These are traditional delicacies in parts of the US, Canada, and many other countries. They are consumed after removal of the outer membrane, then breaded and fried or grilled.

posts.post_title: Sweet Bread — Common Organ
posts.post_content: Which of the following is commonly known as sweet bread?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both Thymus and Pancreas

Both Thymus and Pancreas are commonly known as Sweet Bread.

Thymus vs Pancreas as Sweet Bread
  • Thymus → Neck / Throat / Gullet sweet bread (located in the throat/chest area)
  • Pancreas → Heart / Stomach / Gut / Belly sweet bread (located near the stomach)

In culinary practice, veal sweetbreads (from calves) and lamb sweetbreads are most prized. They are considered organ meats (variety meats) and are prepared by blanching, peeling, and then grilling or pan-frying.

Note on Spleen

The spleen is not called sweet bread — it is simply called spleen or melt in culinary terminology.

posts.post_title: Most Common Stunning Method for Cattle and Buffalo
posts.post_content: Most widely used method of stunning in case of cattle & buffalo is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Mechanical Stunning

The most widely used method of stunning for cattle and buffalo is Mechanical Stunning using a Captive Bolt Pistol or Percussion Stunner.

Species-Wise Preferred Stunning Method
  • Cattle & Buffalo: Mechanical stunning (captive bolt pistol / percussion stunner)
  • Pigs: Chemical/Gas stunning (CO2) — commercial method
  • Sheep, Goat, Pigs: Electrical stunning (Elther apparatus)
  • Poultry: Electric water bath stunning
Why Mechanical Is Preferred for Large Bovines

Cattle and buffaloes have thick skulls that are resistant to electrical current. The captive bolt pistol delivers a precise mechanical impact to the brain (frontal bone), reliably inducing immediate unconsciousness. Electrical stunning is less reliable in large bovines due to thick skull and high body mass.

posts.post_title: PSE Meat — Most Common Species
posts.post_content: Pale, Soft & Exudative (PSE) meat is common in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Pig

PSE (Pale, Soft & Exudative) meat is most commonly found in pigs (pork). It is also known as Watery Pork.

Why PSE Occurs in Pigs

PSE meat develops in stress-susceptible pigs when the muscle pH falls very rapidly (to 5.8–5.6) while the carcass is still warm (above 35°C) immediately after slaughter. This rapid pH decline, combined with high temperature, causes protein denaturation — resulting in poor water-binding capacity, pale colour, and soft/exudative texture.

Key Features of PSE Meat
  • Lower water-binding properties → loses weight rapidly during cooking
  • Leads to decreased processing yields
  • Colour: pale/greyish-pink instead of normal greyish-pink of pork
  • Texture: soft and watery
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Cattle → prone to DFD (Dark, Firm & Dry) meat, not PSE
  • Buffalo → also prone to DFD, not PSE
  • Goat → not commonly associated with PSE

posts.post_title: Fat Recovery from Dead Carcass
posts.post_content: Recovery of fat from the dead carcass is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Rendering

Rendering is the process of recovering fat (and other by-products) from dead or condemned carcasses by applying heat to melt and separate the fat.

By-Product Processing Terms
  • Rendering → Recovery of fat from dead/condemned carcass
  • Shammoying → Tanning sheep skin with fish oil to make it soft and pliable
  • Flaying → Removal of skin/hide from the carcass
  • Bruising → Haemorrhage/injury to tissues (not a recovery process)

Rendered fats are used in manufacturing soap, lubricants and animal feed. The solid residue after rendering is used as meat meal (animal protein supplement).

posts.post_title: Protein Content of Chicken Meat
posts.post_content: The protein content of the chicken egg is 13% while protein content of chicken meat is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 21%

Chicken meat contains approximately 21% protein, while the chicken egg contains about 13% protein.

Proximate Composition of Meat (General)

The standard composition of animal meat is: 72% water and 28% dry matter (DM). The DM consists of:

  • Protein: 21%
  • Fat: 6%
  • Ash (minerals): 1%
Why Chicken Meat Has More Protein Than Egg

Muscle tissue (meat) is primarily composed of contractile proteins (actin, myosin, etc.) and thus has a higher protein content per 100g than egg, which contains a proportionally higher fat fraction in the yolk. Lean muscle = high protein, low fat. Egg = moderate protein, significant fat (yolk lipids).

posts.post_title: Best Stunning Method for Pigs
posts.post_content: The most suitable method of stunning in pigs is:

_aimcq_options.text: No stunning is used for pigs

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Chemical (CO2) Stunning

The most suitable method of stunning for pigs is Chemical (Gas) Stunning using CO2 gas.

CO2 Stunning Parameters for Pigs
  • Gas concentration: 70% CO2 + 30% O2
  • Exposure time: 45 seconds
  • Mechanism: CO2 blocks nerve endings → animal becomes unconscious without panic or struggle
Advantages of CO2 Stunning in Pigs
  • Reduces stress and struggling (important to prevent PSE meat)
  • No physical handling required → lower risk of injury
  • Suitable for high-throughput commercial pig slaughter
  • Reduces incidence of petechial haemorrhages (splash) compared to electrical stunning
Note on Electrical Stunning in Pigs

Electrical stunning can also be used for pigs but may cause 'splash' (petechial haemorrhages in subcutaneous tissue) if current is too high or if the animal is not bled within 30 seconds.

posts.post_title: PSE Meat — Alternative Name
posts.post_content: PSE meat is also known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Watery Pork

PSE meat (Pale, Soft & Exudative) is commonly called Watery Pork because it predominantly occurs in pigs and has a characteristically watery/exudative texture.

Why Is It Called Watery?

The exudate (drip) is caused by protein denaturation due to rapid pH fall in warm post-slaughter muscles. Denatured proteins can no longer hold water within the muscle fibres, so free water (drip) seeps out — hence the name watery pork.

PSE vs DFD — Quick Comparison
  • PSE (Watery Pork): Rapid pH fall → pale, soft, exudative → common in pig
  • DFD (Dark Cutting Beef): No/minimal pH fall → dark, firm, dry → common in cattle/buffalo

posts.post_title: Tanning Sheep Skin with Fish Oil
posts.post_content: The process of tanning sheep skin with fish oil to make it soft & pliable is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Shammoying

Shammoying (also spelled Chamoiseing) is the process of tanning sheep skin with fish oil to make it soft and pliable. The product — chamois leather — is used in cleaning, polishing, and as a soft leather good.

Skin/Hide Processing Terms
  • Shammoying → Tanning sheep skin with fish oil
  • Flaying → Removal of hide/skin from carcass
  • Rendering → Recovery of fat from dead carcass by heat
  • Hide → Skin of cattle & buffalo
  • Rind → Skin of pig
  • Sole leather → Obtained from the butt area of hide

posts.post_title: Ultimate pH of Meat — Exact Value
posts.post_content: The ultimate pH of meat is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 5.6

The ultimate (final) pH of normal meat is 5.6 (range: 5.5–5.7).

Post-Slaughter pH Cascade
  1. Living muscle pH: ~7.2
  2. Slaughter → anaerobic glycolysis begins → glycogen → lactic acid
  3. pH falls progressively over 6–24 hours
  4. Ultimate pH (when glycogen is exhausted): 5.5–5.7 (typically 5.6)
Deviation from Normal Ultimate pH
  • pH >6.0 → DFD meat (insufficient glycogen → too little lactic acid)
  • Rapid fall to 5.8–5.6 in warm carcass → PSE meat
  • pH 5.6 in cold carcass → Normal

pH 7.2 is the living muscle pH (pre-slaughter physiological pH) — choosing this indicates confusion between living tissue pH and post-mortem ultimate pH.

posts.post_title: CO2 Pre-Slaughter Anaesthesia — Species
posts.post_content: Pre-slaughter anaesthesia with CO2 is mainly used for stunning in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Pig

Pre-slaughter anaesthesia with CO2 gas is mainly used for stunning in pigs. This is also the commercial method for pig stunning.

CO2 Stunning — Full Details
  • Species: Pigs (primarily)
  • Concentration: 70% CO2 + 30% O2
  • Duration: 45 seconds
  • Mode of action: CO2 blocks nerve endings in the brain → unconsciousness without pain
  • Function in meat quality: Reduces stress → reduces glycogen depletion → reduces PSE incidence
Why Not Used in Cattle?

CO2 stunning is impractical for large animals like cattle and buffalo because of the large enclosed chamber required and their resistance to anaesthetic gases. Mechanical stunning (captive bolt) is more practical and reliable for bovines.

posts.post_title: DFD Meat — Most Common Species
posts.post_content: Dry, Firm & Dark (DFD) meat is common in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Cattle

DFD (Dry, Firm & Dark) meat is most commonly found in cattle (beef). It is also called Dark Cutting Beef.

Why DFD Occurs

DFD occurs when animals have been excessively fatigued during transportation and lairage, or when they have not been fed for a prolonged period before slaughter. As a result, most muscle glycogen is already depleted before slaughter. Since there is insufficient glycogen, lactic acid cannot be produced and the ultimate muscle pH does not fall below 6.0 (normal ultimate pH is 5.5–5.7).

Effect of High pH on Meat
  • High pH causes muscle proteins to retain most of their bound water
  • Proteins absorb most light striking the meat surface → giving a dark appearance
  • Texture: firm and dry on the surface
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Pig → prone to PSE, not DFD
  • Buffalo → can also show DFD but less commonly cited than cattle in textbooks
  • Goat → not commonly associated with DFD

posts.post_title: By-Products — Heparin, Rennet, Pepsin
posts.post_content: Which of the following sentences is/are true?

_aimcq_options.text: Heparin is extracted from cattle lungs
Rennet is prepared from abomasum of suckling calf
Pepsin is extracted from mucosal lining of pig stomach

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

All three statements are correct about animal by-products used in industry:

Animal By-Products — Industrial Uses
  • Heparin → Anticoagulant drug; extracted from cattle lungs (and also from pig intestinal mucosa)
  • Rennet → Milk-clotting enzyme; prepared from the abomasum (fourth stomach) of suckling calf — used in cheese making
  • Pepsin → Proteolytic enzyme; extracted from the mucosal lining of pig stomach — used in food industry and as digestive enzyme
  • Hyaluronidase → Extracted from Bull or Ram testes — used as spreading factor in medicine
  • Horn raw material → Used to produce gelatin
  • Catgut (absorbable suture) → Obtained from submucosa of small intestine of sheep

posts.post_title: Major Amino Acid in Collagen
posts.post_content: An amino acid which forms a major part of collagen is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Glycine

Glycine forms the major part of collagen. In fact, every third residue in collagen's triple-helix structure is glycine (Gly-X-Y repeating unit), making it the most abundant amino acid in collagen — approximately 33% of all residues.

Collagen Amino Acid Profile
  • Rich in: Glycine (~33%), Proline, Hydroxyproline
  • Deficient in: Cysteine and Tryptophan (essential amino acids — hence collagen is a nutritionally poor/incomplete protein)
Why Glycine Is Critical

Glycine's small side chain (just H) is essential — only glycine is small enough to fit inside the tight central helix of the collagen triple helix structure. Substitution of any glycine by a larger amino acid causes diseases like Osteogenesis Imperfecta (brittle bone disease).

posts.post_title: Veal — Definition
posts.post_content: Veal is the meat of:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Calf

Veal is the meat obtained from a calf (young cattle, usually less than 3 months old). Its colour is brownish pink and it has no intra-muscular fat (no marbling).

Meat Terminology Table
  • Calf → Veal (brownish pink, no intra-muscular fat)
  • Cattle → Beef (cherry red, ~55% dressing %)
  • Buffalo → Carabeef / Buffen (cherry red, ~57% dressing %)
  • Sheep → Mutton (light to dark red, ~50% dressing %)
  • Goat → Chevon (light red, ~49% dressing %)
  • Pig → Pork (greyish pink, ~72% dressing %)
  • Deer & Antelope → Venison
  • Rabbit → Game

posts.post_title: Myofibrillar Protein Solubility (Detailed)
posts.post_content: Myofibrillar proteins are soluble in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Salt only

Myofibrillar proteins (Actin, Myosin, Tropomyosin, Troponins) are salt-soluble only — they require a high ionic strength (salt solution) for solubilization and are NOT soluble in plain water.

Three Meat Protein Groups and Solubility
  • Myofibrillar proteins: Salt-soluble (e.g., Actin, Myosin, Tropomyosin) → 50–60% of muscle proteins
  • Sarcoplasmic proteins: Water-soluble AND salt-soluble (e.g., Myoglobin, glycolytic enzymes) → 30–35% of muscle proteins
  • Stromal proteins: Insoluble in both water and salt (e.g., Collagen, Reticulin, Elastin) → 10–15% of muscle proteins

In sausage making, addition of salt extracts myofibrillar proteins (especially myosin) which are critical for binding and emulsification in meat products.

posts.post_title: Collagen — Amino Acid Composition
posts.post_content: Collagen is a rich source of:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Glycine, Proline, Hydroxyproline

Collagen is a rich source of Glycine, Proline, and Hydroxyproline. These three amino acids are uniquely abundant in collagen and are responsible for its triple-helix structure.

Collagen's Unique Features
  • Glycine (~33%): Every 3rd residue; essential for helix formation
  • Proline and Hydroxyproline (~22%): Stabilize the triple helix; Hydroxyproline is almost exclusive to collagen — it is used as a marker for collagen content in food analysis
  • Deficient in: Cysteine and Tryptophan
Hydroxyproline as a Collagen Marker

Since hydroxyproline is found almost exclusively in collagen, measuring hydroxyproline content in food products is a standard analytical technique to determine collagen/connective tissue content.

posts.post_title: Bright Red Colour of Meat
posts.post_content: The bright red colour of meat is due to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Oxymyoglobin

The bright red (cherry red) colour of fresh meat is due to Oxymyoglobin (MbO₂) — formed when myoglobin reacts with oxygen.

Myoglobin Colour States
  • Myoglobin (Mb) — Purplish-red colour (in absence of oxygen, e.g., deep inside packed meat)
  • Oxymyoglobin (MbO₂) — Bright red / cherry red colour (on the surface when fresh meat is exposed to oxygen — this is called Bloom)
  • Metmyoglobin (MMb) — Brown colour (formed by oxidation; seen in old/stale meat)
  • Nitroso-haemochromogen — Pink colour (in cured meat after smoking/heating)
  • Carboxymyoglobin — Bright cherry red (formed with CO gas; used in modified atmosphere packaging)

Bloom = The bright red colour of fresh meat due to oxymyoglobin — it is a quality indicator consumers look for.

posts.post_title: Sarcoplasmic Protein Solubility
posts.post_content: Sarcoplasmic proteins (e.g., myoglobin) are soluble in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both water and salt

Sarcoplasmic proteins (e.g., Myoglobin, glycolytic enzymes) are soluble in both water and salt solutions. They are low molecular weight, globular proteins.

Why Sarcoplasmic Proteins Are Both Water- and Salt-Soluble

Sarcoplasmic proteins are inherently hydrophilic (water-loving) with a globular structure. Their surface amino acids are predominantly polar/charged, making them readily soluble in water. Salt further enhances their solubility by ionic interactions.

Practical Implication

When meat is minced or ground, sarcoplasmic proteins (including myoglobin — the red pigment) leach out readily in the meat drip/exudate. This is why ground/minced meat turns grey/brown faster than intact muscle — surface myoglobin oxidizes to metmyoglobin more readily.

posts.post_title: Amino Acids Deficient in Collagen
posts.post_content: Amino acids deficient in collagen are:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Cysteine, Tryptophan

Collagen is deficient in Cysteine and Tryptophan — both of which are essential amino acids. This makes collagen an incomplete protein nutritionally.

Nutritional Significance
  • Diets high in collagen-rich cuts (tendons, skin, cartilage) are nutritionally inadequate if used as the sole protein source
  • Tryptophan is the precursor to serotonin and niacin; its deficiency causes Pellagra
  • Cysteine is involved in antioxidant defence (part of glutathione)
Blood Meal Contrast

Blood meal is a rich source of Lysine — making it a valuable supplement for diets deficient in lysine (e.g., maize-based diets). Compare this with collagen which lacks cysteine and tryptophan.

posts.post_title: Brown Colour of Meat
posts.post_content: The brown colour of meat is due to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Metmyoglobin

The brown colour of old/stale meat is due to Metmyoglobin (MMb), formed when myoglobin is oxidized (Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺).

Myoglobin Pigment Summary
  • Myoglobin → Purplish-red (deoxygenated state)
  • Oxymyoglobin → Bright red (oxygenated — fresh meat surface)
  • Metmyoglobin → Brown (oxidized — stale or old meat)
  • Nitroso-haemochromogen → Pink (cured and cooked meat)

Metmyoglobin formation is an indicator of meat deterioration. Reducing agents (like ascorbic acid/Vitamin C) can convert MMb back to Mb, temporarily restoring red colour.

posts.post_title: Stromal Protein Solubility
posts.post_content: Stromal proteins (e.g., collagen, reticulin & elastin) are insoluble in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both water and salt

Stromal (connective tissue) proteins — Collagen, Reticulin, and Elastin — are almost insoluble in both water and salt solutions. They are fibrous structural proteins.

Collagen Facts
  • Rich in: Glycine, Proline, and Hydroxyproline
  • Deficient in: Cysteine and Tryptophan (essential amino acids)
  • Bone collagen → called Ossein or Demineralized bone
  • Gelatin → obtained by partial hydrolysis (boiling in water) of collagen; a crude form is Glue
  • Collagen is responsible for the toughness of meat — meat from older animals is tougher because collagen crosslinks increase with age
Why Stromal Proteins Are Insoluble

Their fibrous triple-helix structure and extensive crosslinking make them resistant to normal solvents. Only prolonged heating (moist heat cooking) converts collagen to soluble gelatin.

posts.post_title: Blood Meal — Amino Acid Content
posts.post_content: Blood meal is a rich source of:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Lysine

Blood meal is an exceptionally rich source of Lysine — one of the most important essential amino acids often deficient in cereal/grain-based diets.

Blood Meal Facts
  • Crude Protein: ~80% — one of the highest protein feed ingredients
  • Rich in: Lysine (especially), Isoleucine is present but relatively low
  • Conversion ratio: 5:1 (5 kg raw blood → 1 kg blood meal)
  • Used as: Protein supplement in livestock and poultry feed
Why Lysine Matters

Lysine is the first limiting amino acid in maize/corn-based diets. Blood meal supplementation effectively corrects this deficiency. Lysine is critical for muscle protein synthesis, calcium absorption, and immune function.

posts.post_title: Solubility of Myofibrillar Proteins
posts.post_content: Myofibrillar proteins are soluble in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Salt

Myofibrillar proteins (e.g., Actin, Myosin, Tropomyosin) are salt-soluble — they require a salt solution (high ionic strength) for extraction.

Meat Protein Solubility Chart
  • Myofibrillar proteins (Actin, Myosin, Tropomyosin, Troponins, Desmin, Connectins) → Salt-soluble; constitute 50–60% of total muscle proteins
  • Sarcoplasmic proteins (Myoglobin, glycolytic enzymes) → Water-soluble (and also salt-soluble); constitute 30–35% of total muscle proteins
  • Stromal/Connective tissue proteins (Collagen, Reticulin, Elastin) → Almost insoluble in both water and salt; constitute 10–15% of total muscle proteins

This solubility property is exploited in sausage/emulsion-type meat product manufacturing — salt extracts myofibrillar proteins which act as emulsifiers.

posts.post_title: Horn Raw Material — Industrial Use
posts.post_content: Horn raw material is used to produce:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Gelatin

Horn raw material (horn core) is used to produce Gelatin. Horns are composed of keratin on the outside and bone on the inside (horn core). The bone/collagen component is processed to yield gelatin.

Animal By-Products → Industrial Products
  • Horn raw material → Gelatin
  • Collagen (bone/hide) → Gelatin, Glue
  • Blood → Blood meal (rich in Lysine), Heparin, Albumin
  • Bile → Pharmaceuticals
  • Fat (technical) → Soap, lubricants
  • Bone → Bone meal, Bone ash, Ossein (demineralised bone collagen)
  • Bone conversion rate: 3:1 (raw bone to bone meal)
  • Blood meal conversion rate: 5:1 (raw blood to blood meal)

posts.post_title: Cause of PSE Condition in Meat
posts.post_content: PSE condition is a direct result of:

_aimcq_options.text: Very less fall of muscle pH

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Rapid fall of muscle pH

PSE meat is a direct result of a very rapid fall in muscle pH (to 5.8–5.6) while the carcass temperature is still high (above 35°C) after slaughter. This combination of low pH + high temperature causes excessive protein denaturation.

pH Comparison: PSE vs DFD vs Normal Meat
  • Normal meat ultimate pH: 5.5–5.7 (gradual fall)
  • PSE meat: Rapid pH drop to 5.8–5.6 while muscle is still warm → protein denaturation → pale, soft, exudative
  • DFD meat: pH does not fall below 6.0 (insufficient glycogen) → dark, firm, dry

Mechanism: Rapid glycogenolysis → rapid lactic acid production → rapid pH fall → denaturation of sarcoplasmic and myofibrillar proteins → reduced water-holding capacity → exudate/drip.

posts.post_title: Best Age of Broiler for Tandoori Chicken
posts.post_content: For tandoori chicken, the best age of broiler is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 6 weeks

For Tandoori chicken, the best age of broiler is 6 weeks. At 6 weeks, the broiler achieves an optimum body weight and meat-to-bone ratio suitable for tandoor cooking.

Broiler Age for Different Preparations
  • Tandoori chicken: 6-week-old broiler
  • Chicken Barbecue: Broiler with ~750 g dressed weight is preferred
Meat-to-Bone Ratio in Broiler

Meat : Bone ratio in a dressed broiler = 4:1

Why Not Other Ages?
  • 4 weeks → Too young; insufficient meat yield
  • 8 weeks → Older broilers tend to be tougher; not optimal for tandoor
  • 2 weeks → Far too young; not suitable for processing

posts.post_title: Slaughter Without Prior Stunning
posts.post_content: Slaughter without prior stunning is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Ritual Slaughter

Ritual (Religious) Slaughter is performed without prior stunning. In humane/scientific slaughter, stunning is mandatory before bleeding.

Methods of Slaughter
  • Humane / Scientific slaughter: Animal is stunned first (mechanical/electrical/chemical), then bled — avoids pain and suffering
  • Ritual slaughter: No prior stunning — performed according to religious prescription
    • Jewish method (Schechita)
    • Muslim method (Halal)
    • Sikh method (Jhatka)
    • Evernazine method (Neck Stab)
Key Distinction

Stunning is performed only in humane slaughter, not in ritual slaughter. This is a critical distinction in meat hygiene examinations.

posts.post_title: Inter-Muscular Fat Terminology
posts.post_content: Intra-muscular fat is known as marbling of meat while inter-muscular fat is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Seam Fat

Inter-muscular fat (fat deposited between muscles) is known as Seam Fat.

Fat Terminology in Meat Science
  • Intra-muscular fat → Marbling (fat within muscle fibres; maximum in mutton and beef)
  • Inter-muscular fat → Seam Fat (fat between muscles)
  • Subcutaneous fat → fat under the skin; maximum in pork and poultry
  • Ruffle fat → fat around the kidney (peri-renal fat)
  • Caul fat → Omental fat (fat around the stomach/omentum)
  • Lard → Pig fat (processed)
  • Tallow → Processed fat from cattle (made from suet)
  • Suet → Raw beef or mutton fat (especially around kidneys)

posts.post_title: Ultimate pH of Meat
posts.post_content: Ultimate pH of meat is in the range of:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 5.5 – 5.7

The ultimate pH of normal meat ranges from 5.5 to 5.7. The exact figure cited in most textbooks is 5.6.

Post-Mortem pH Changes in Muscle
  • Living muscle pH: ~7.2 (normal physiological pH)
  • Immediately after slaughter: pH begins to fall as glycogen is converted to lactic acid (glycolysis continues post-mortem)
  • Ultimate pH (normal): 5.5–5.7 (most commonly cited as 5.6)
  • PSE meat: Rapid pH fall to 5.8–5.6 while muscle is still warm
  • DFD meat: pH does not fall below 6.0 (insufficient glycogen)

The ultimate pH affects water-holding capacity, colour, tenderness, and microbial shelf life of meat.

posts.post_title: Back Bleeding / Over-Sticking
posts.post_content: Back bleeding / over-sticking is common in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Pig slaughtered with Evernazine method

Back bleeding (over-sticking) is a condition where the knife penetrates too far into the chest cavity during sticking/bleeding, causing blood to be aspirated into the thoracic cavity and contaminating the lungs.

Why It Occurs in Evernazine Method in Pigs

In the Evernazine method, a double-edged knife (Puntilla) is used to sever the neck at the occipito-atlantal joint. The sticking procedure in pigs, combined with the Evernazine method's approach, increases the risk of the knife penetrating too far — leading to back bleeding.

Consequences of Back Bleeding
  • Blood accumulates in thoracic cavity
  • Lungs become blood-contaminated
  • Pluck (lungs + trachea + heart) is condemned
  • Represents economic loss and hygiene concern

posts.post_title: Bacterial Growth Temperature Ranges
posts.post_content: Which of the following statements is/are true about optimum growth temperature of bacteria?

_aimcq_options.text: Optimum growth temperature for psychrophilic bacteria is below 20°C
Mesophilic bacteria grow well in 20–45°C temperature
Thermophilic bacteria grow well above 45°C temperature

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

All three statements are correct regarding bacterial growth temperature ranges.

Bacterial Classification by Growth Temperature
  • Psychrophilic bacteria: Optimum growth below 20°C → responsible for bacterial spoilage in chilled/refrigerated meat
  • Mesophilic bacteria: Optimum growth at 20–45°C → most common pathogens (e.g., Salmonella, E. coli) belong here
  • Thermophilic bacteria: Optimum growth above 45°C → important in canning (e.g., Bacillus stearothermophilus, Clostridium thermosaccharolyticum)

Practical Application in Meat Preservation: Chilling (4°C) does not kill psychrophiles but slows their growth. Freezing (–18°C) stops all microbial growth. Hence chilling is for short-term and freezing for long-term preservation.

posts.post_title: Vitamin C Absence in Food
posts.post_content: Vitamin C is almost absent in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) is almost absent in milk, lean meat, and eggs. These animal-origin foods are not sources of Vitamin C.

Vitamin Distribution in Meat/Animal Products
  • Vitamin C: Absent in lean meat, milk, eggs — found in fruits and vegetables
  • Vitamin B-complex: Lean meat is an excellent source (especially B1, B2, B3, B12)
  • Vitamin B1 (Thiamine): Maximum in Pork (5–10 times more than beef & mutton)
  • Vitamin B12: Found in highest amount in animal meat (especially organ/variety meat)
  • Niacin (B3): Highest in poultry meat
  • Vitamin A: Present in beef and mutton; absent in buffalo meat, chevon, and pork
  • Liver: Richest source of Vitamin A

posts.post_title: Use of Puntilla Knife
posts.post_content: Puntilla is used in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Evernazine Method

Puntilla is the double-edged knife used specifically in the Evernazine method (Neck Stab method) of ritual slaughter.

What Puntilla Does

In the Evernazine method, the Puntilla is used to:

  • Sever the neck at the occipito-atlantal joint
  • Sever the medulla oblongata

Because the medulla oblongata is damaged, bleeding remains incomplete (similar to the Jhatka method).

Slaughter Methods — Key Instruments
  • Evernazine (Neck Stab): Puntilla (double-edged knife)
  • Mechanical stunning: Captive bolt pistol / Percussion stunner
  • Electrical stunning: Elther apparatus
  • Chemical stunning: CO2 gas (70% CO2 for 45 seconds)

posts.post_title: Eating of Dog Flesh — Terminology
posts.post_content: Eating of horse flesh is known as hippophagy while eating of dog flesh is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Kynophagy

The practice of eating dog flesh is called Kynophagy (from Greek: kynos = dog + phagein = to eat).

Eating Practice Terminology
  • Hippophagy → eating of horse flesh (hippos = horse)
  • Kynophagy → eating of dog flesh (kynos = dog)
  • Coprophagy → eating of faeces (copros = faeces) — not a human food practice
  • Caninephagia / Canophagy → incorrect/non-standard terms

These terms appear in competitive veterinary exams to test knowledge of technical food terminology.

posts.post_title: Maximum Thiamine Content in Meat
posts.post_content: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) content is maximum in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Pork

Pork contains the maximum Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) among all meats — approximately 5–10 times more thiamine than beef and mutton.

Vitamin B Distribution in Meat
  • Vitamin B1 (Thiamine): Maximum in Pork (5–10× more than beef & mutton)
  • Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin) & B12: Higher in beef and mutton
  • Folic acid & Vitamin B12: Higher in beef and mutton
  • Niacin (B3): Highest in poultry meat
  • Vitamin B-complex overall: Maximum in pork

Vitamin B1 is important for energy metabolism and nerve function. Deficiency causes Beriberi. Pork is thus the best dietary meat source of Thiamine.

posts.post_title: Food Forbidden in Islam
posts.post_content: In Muslims, consumption of which of the following is forbidden?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

In Islam, consumption of dead animals (carrion), blood, and pork is forbidden (Haram). These prohibitions are mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:173).

Halal vs Haram in Meat
  • Haram (forbidden): Dead animals, blood, pork, animals not slaughtered in the name of Allah
  • Halal method: The animal must be slaughtered by a Muslim, in the name of Allah, with the head facing Mecca, by severing carotid arteries and jugular veins in one swift stroke without prior stunning
Comparison with Jewish Prohibition

Jews are also forbidden from eating pork — as a safeguard against Tapeworm infection (Taenia solium). Both religions prohibit pork, but for different stated reasons.

posts.post_title: Buffalo Meat — Alternative Names
posts.post_content: Buffalo meat is also known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both Carabeef and Buffen

Buffalo meat is known by two names: Carabeef and Buffen.

Buffalo Meat Facts
  • Colour: Cherry red (same as beef)
  • Dressing percentage: ~57% (highest among red meats)
  • Shelf life at –18°C: 6 months (same as beef, mutton and chevon)
  • India is one of the world's largest exporters of carabeef
  • In India, buffaloes are slaughtered predominantly by the Halal method
Vitamin A in Buffalo Meat

Vitamin A is absent in buffalo meat (present in beef and mutton but absent in buffalo meat, chevon/goat meat, and pork).

posts.post_title: Mineral Deficiency in Meat
posts.post_content: Meat is generally a good source of all minerals except:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Calcium

Meat is a good source of most minerals except Calcium. Lean meat is particularly poor in calcium content.

Mineral Content of Meat
  • Calcium: Very low in lean meat — dairy products and leafy vegetables are the main dietary sources
  • Iron: Meat is an excellent source of haem iron (the most bioavailable form of iron)
  • Phosphorus: Good source in meat
  • Zinc: Red meat is an excellent source of zinc
  • Potassium, Magnesium: Present in decent amounts in meat

Haem vs Non-haem Iron: Iron in meat (myoglobin-bound = haem iron) is 2–3 times more bioavailable than non-haem iron from plant sources. This makes meat especially valuable in preventing iron-deficiency anaemia.

posts.post_title: Kosher Stamp Location
posts.post_content: Carcass fit for Jewish consumption is stamped with:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Kosher seal on brisket

A carcass fit for Jewish consumption is stamped with the Kosher seal on the brisket (the chest/breast area of the carcass).

Kosher vs Terepha
  • Kosher → Carcass fit for Jewish consumption → stamped with Kosher seal on brisket
  • Terepha → Carcass found unfit for Jewish consumption after post-mortem examination
Schochet — Role in Inspection

The Schochet (Jewish ritual slaughterer) not only performs the slaughter but also conducts a post-mortem examination. If the carcass shows any lesions (wounds, disease, abnormalities), it is declared Terepha and cannot be sold as Kosher meat.

posts.post_title: Prime Pork — Definition
posts.post_content: The carcass of castrated male & virgin female of pig is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Prime Pork

The carcass of a castrated male pig and virgin female pig is specifically referred to as Prime Pork.

Pork Terminology
  • Pork → Generic name for pig meat
  • Prime Pork → Carcass of castrated male (barrow) & virgin female (gilt) pig
  • Bacon → Preserved pork prepared from the sides and back of a pig; preserved by curing with brine
  • Ham → Meat from the thigh or buttocks of a pig
  • Lard → Processed pig fat

Prime pork is preferred for its superior meat quality — castration removes the boar taint (urine-like odour) associated with intact male pigs.

posts.post_title: Lean Meat — Vitamin Content
posts.post_content: Lean meat is an excellent source of which vitamin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Vitamin B-complex

Lean meat is an excellent source of Vitamin B-complex vitamins, particularly B1 (thiamine), B2 (riboflavin), B3 (niacin), and B12 (cobalamin).

Vitamins in Lean Meat
  • Vitamin B-complex: Abundant — lean meat is one of the best dietary sources
  • Vitamin B12: Exclusively found in animal products; meat is the primary source
  • Vitamin C: Almost absent in lean meat
  • Vitamin A: Present in beef and mutton but absent in buffalo meat, chevon, and pork
  • Vitamin D & E: Present in small amounts

Vitamins lost during cold sterilization include: B1, B2, and C. This is important for understanding nutritional changes during meat preservation.

posts.post_title: Incomplete Bleeding Due to Medulla Oblongata Damage
posts.post_content: In which of the following methods of ritual slaughter does bleeding remain incomplete due to damage of medulla oblongata?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Jhatka & Evernazine method

In both the Jhatka method and the Evernazine method, bleeding remains incomplete because the medulla oblongata is damaged/severed during slaughter.

Why Medulla Oblongata Damage Causes Incomplete Bleeding

The medulla oblongata controls the cardiovascular centre (heart rate and vasomotor tone). When it is severed/damaged, the heart stops pumping effectively, so blood cannot be fully expelled from the carcass — resulting in incomplete bleeding (blood remains in meat).

Slaughter Methods — Bleeding Completeness
  • Halal method: Jugular veins & carotid arteries severed → complete bleeding → best blood drainage
  • Jewish method (Schechita): Similar to Halal → complete bleeding
  • Jhatka method: Neck severed in one stroke → medulla damaged → incomplete bleeding
  • Evernazine method: Puntilla severs occipito-atlantal joint + medulla → incomplete bleeding

posts.post_title: Animal Fat Terminology
posts.post_content: Which of the following sentences is/are correct about animal fat?

_aimcq_options.text: Pig fat is known as lard
Raw beef or mutton fat is known as suet
Omental fat is known as caul fat

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

All three statements about animal fat are correct.

Complete Animal Fat Terminology
  • Pig fat → Lard (rendered pig fat used in cooking)
  • Raw beef or mutton fat (especially kidney fat) → Suet
  • Omental fat (fat of the omentum/stomach lining) → Caul fat
  • Tallow → Processed fat derived from suet (raw beef/mutton fat)

  • Ruffle fat → Fat around the kidney
  • Technical fat → Used in manufacturing of soap, lubricants (not edible)

posts.post_title: Measuring Firmness of Meat
posts.post_content: The firmness of meat is measured by:

_aimcq_options.text: Both shear force apparatus and penetrometer

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both shear force apparatus and penetrometer

The firmness (tenderness) of meat is measured using both the Shear Force Apparatus (Warner-Bratzler Shear) and the Penetrometer.

Instruments Used in Meat Quality Assessment
  • Shear Force Apparatus (Warner-Bratzler): Measures the force required to shear through a meat sample — the primary instrument for objective tenderness measurement
  • Penetrometer: Measures firmness/consistency by pressing a probe into meat
  • Densitometer / Electric Eye: Used to measure smoke density in a smokehouse
  • Anemometer: Measures wind speed (used in smokehouse air flow)
Meat Consistency by Species
  • Chevon: Very firm
  • Mutton: Firm & dense
  • Beef: Fairly firm
  • Pork: Very soft

posts.post_title: Instruments for Mechanical Stunning
posts.post_content: Instrument(s) used in mechanical stunning is/are:

_aimcq_options.text: Both captive bolt pistol and percussion stunner

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both captive bolt pistol and percussion stunner

Both the Captive Bolt Pistol and the Percussion Stunner are instruments used in mechanical stunning.

Stunning Methods and Instruments
  • Mechanical stunning: Captive bolt pistol + Percussion stunner → Used mainly for cattle & buffaloes
    Capacity: Captive bolt pistol handles up to 250 cattle/hour
  • Electrical stunning: Elther apparatus (alternating current, 250 mA, 75 volts for 10 seconds) → Used for sheep, goat, pigs, poultry
  • Chemical (Gas) stunning: CO2 chambers (70% CO2 + 30% O2 for 45 seconds) → Most suitable for pigs
Most Widely Used Methods
  • Cattle & buffalo: Mechanical stunning
  • Pigs: Chemical (CO2) stunning
  • Sheep, Goat, Pigs: Electrical stunning
  • Poultry: Electric water bath

posts.post_title: Cooked Testicles — Common Names
posts.post_content: Cooked testicles of calf, lamb & pigs are commonly known as:

_aimcq_options.text: All the above (Rocky mountain oysters, Prairie oysters, Calf fries)

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

Cooked testicles of calf, lamb, and pigs are known by several names: Rocky Mountain Oysters, Prairie Oysters, and Calf Fries.

Variety Meat (Offal) Terminology for Testicles
  • Rocky Mountain Oysters / Prairie Oysters / Calf Fries → Cooked testicles of calf, lamb & pigs
  • Lamb Fries → Cooked testicles specifically of lamb (a subset of the above)
Other Variety Meat Terms
  • Variety meat / Organ meat → organs such as tongue, brain, thymus, heart, liver & kidney

posts.post_title: Sweet Bread — Gland Terminology
posts.post_content: Which statement is true about sweet breads?

_aimcq_options.text: Thymus is known as neck sweet bread
Pancreas is known as gut sweet bread
Parotid gland is known as cheek/ear sweet bread and sublingual glands are known as tongue sweet bread

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: All the above

All three statements about sweet breads are correct.

Complete Sweet Bread Terminology
  • Thymus → Neck sweet bread (also: throat/gullet sweet bread)
  • Pancreas → Gut sweet bread (also: heart/stomach/belly sweet bread)
  • Parotid gland → Cheek/ear sweet bread
  • Sublingual glands → Tongue sweet bread
Why Are They Called Sweet Breads?

The term 'sweetbread' is a culinary term (not anatomical). 'Sweet' refers to the pleasantly mild taste, and 'bread' is derived from the Old English word for flesh. Thymus and Pancreas are the most commonly consumed sweet breads — especially veal and lamb sweetbreads are considered delicacies.

posts.post_title: Jewish Prohibition of Pork — Reason
posts.post_content: Consumption of pork was strictly prohibited for Jews as a safeguard against:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Tapeworm

Pork was prohibited for Jews as a safeguard against Tapeworm (Taenia solium) infection. Pork is the primary intermediate host for Taenia solium (pork tapeworm).

Measly Pork and Cysticercosis
  • Measly pork → Pork infected with cysts (Cysticercus cellulosae) of Taenia solium
  • Measly beef → Beef infected with Cysticercus bovis (cattle tapeworm — Taenia saginata)
  • Consuming infected raw/undercooked pork can cause cysticercosis or taeniasis in humans
  • Neurocysticercosis (brain tapeworm) is a serious complication from consuming Cysticercus cellulosae
Why Thoroughness Matters

Even today, thorough cooking (internal temperature ≥63°C) destroys tapeworm cysts in pork. The Jewish/Islamic prohibition thus had a strong public health basis in pre-refrigeration times.
